Definition: from G2596 and G2827; to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table:--(make) sit down (at meat).
BiblicalUsage: To recline is to take your place at the table, and Jesus is always doing it: making the five thousand sit down in companies, teaching the guest not to take the highest room, reclining at Emmaus to break the bread, and lying at meat in a Pharisee's house while a sinful woman wept at His feet. The table is where He teaches, where He feeds, and where He is recognised.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the table is one of the holiest places in the Gospels, because Jesus chose it again and again to show us the kingdom. I hold that the lowest place is the safest seat, since the Host Himself promises to come and serve those who take it.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand; The Road to Emmaus
